title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: how many excess withdrawal fees may still be charged in a reconciled cycle
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Savings & Money Market Accounts account from which overdraft protection transfers have been made, when the excess withdrawal fees of a statement cycle are reconciled. It fixes how many more excess withdrawal fees the tier's per-cycle maximum still allows in that cycle.

## Policy clause

Every excess withdrawal fee entry posted in the cycle, refunded or not, counts toward the tier's most excess withdrawal fees per cycle, in the same way that the number of excess withdrawal fees posted in a cycle is counted. So the fees that may still be charged in the cycle are that maximum less every such entry, and never fewer than none.

## Basis of decision

- **Authority.** The fee entries and their statement cycle are read from the savings account's transaction record; the maximum is the account tier's value.
- **Object correlation.** Every excess withdrawal fee entry of the cycle counts, whether it has since been refunded on any ground or not.

## Worked cases (hypothetical tier: at most 4 excess withdrawal fees per cycle; illustrative, not a tier value)

| Excess withdrawal fee entries posted in the cycle | Of which refunded | Fees that may still be charged |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 3 |
| 3 | 1, as a bank error | 1; the refunded entry still counts toward the maximum |
| 4 | 2 | 0 |
| 5 | 0 | 0; never fewer than none |

## Points of judgement

**Wrong reading:** "A fee refunded as a bank error frees its place under the maximum." **Correct basis:** every fee entry posted in the cycle, refunded or not, counts toward the maximum.

**On a tier whose maximum is 0, can any fee still be charged?** No; the maximum less any number of entries is never more than none.
